intro: Exam-style performance-based tasks for the CCNA: subnetting, VLANs, ACLs, OSPF, EtherChannel and IPv6.

questions.title: Subnet calculations
questions.scenario: Document a host's subnet and plan a split of a /24 into four equal subnets.

activities.title: Split 192.168.4.0/24 into four equal subnets
activities.prompt: Give the prefix and the network address of each subnet that follows 192.168.4.0.

questions.explanation: /27 = block size 32 in the last octet. 77 falls in 64-95, so network .64, broadcast .95, hosts .65 to .94 (30 usable). Four subnets need 2 borrowed bits: /26, blocks of 64 (.0, .64, .128, .192); the last broadcast is .255.

questions.title: VLAN and trunk commands
questions.scenario: You are configuring a new access switch. Recall the IOS commands for each task.

activities.title: Type the command
activities.prompt: Enter the full IOS command (abbreviations are accepted where IOS allows them).

rows.label: Place an access port in VLAN 20
Show a summary of VLANs and their access ports
Show trunk ports with allowed and native VLANs
Change the trunk native VLAN to 99

questions.explanation: Access ports use switchport mode access and switchport access vlan N. Trunks use switchport mode trunk; the native VLAN is changed with switchport trunk native vlan N and must match on both ends. show vlan brief and show interfaces trunk are the key verification commands.

questions.title: Build the ACL
questions.scenario: Server 10.1.1.10 must be protected. The current ACL permits everything. Rewrite it with these requirements: the sales subnet 192.168.10.0/24 may use HTTPS; the help desk subnet 192.168.20.0/24 may ping the server; only host 192.168.30.4 may use SSH; deny everything else.

activities.title: Edit the ACL
activities.prompt: Edit, add, delete and reorder rules. Use Any, a single IP, or CIDR like 10.1.1.0/24. Ports can be a number, a range (8000-8080) or a list (80,443). Everything not allowed is denied.

tests.label: Help desk host to server TCP 443
Help desk host ping (ICMP) to server

questions.explanation: An ACL is checked top to bottom, first match wins, with an implicit deny at the end. Use TCP 443 for sales, ICMP for the help desk subnet and a host-specific TCP 22 entry for the admin. Extended ACLs go close to the source.

questions.title: OSPF neighbor states and timers
questions.scenario: Two routers will not form an OSPF adjacency. Review how it works.

activities.title: Order the OSPF neighbor states
activities.prompt: Put the states in the order a neighbor passes through them.

rows.label: Default hello interval on a broadcast network (seconds)
Default dead interval on a broadcast network (seconds)
Multicast address for all OSPF routers
Multicast address for DRs and BDRs

questions.explanation: Neighbors move Down, Init, 2-Way, ExStart, Exchange, Loading, Full. On Ethernet, hello 10 s and dead 40 s must match, as must area, subnet and authentication. OSPF uses 224.0.0.5 (all routers) and 224.0.0.6 (DR/BDR), AD 110.

questions.title: EtherChannel and spanning tree
questions.scenario: Plan a link bundle between two switches and harden the access ports.

activities.title: Does this pair of modes form an EtherChannel?
activities.prompt: Drag each combination to the right group.

rows.label: Command to enable Rapid PVST+ (global configuration)
Feature that err-disables a PortFast port if a BPDU arrives (two words)

questions.explanation: Both ends must use the same protocol family: LACP active/passive, PAgP desirable/auto or static on. Two passive or two auto ends never negotiate. The default bridge priority is 32768; BPDU guard protects PortFast edge ports.

questions.title: IPv6 address types and services
questions.scenario: Sort the addresses found in a routing table, then recall IPv6 basics.

activities.title: Identify the address type
activities.prompt: Drag each address to its type.

rows.label: Protocol that replaces ARP in IPv6 (acronym)
Command that enables IPv6 routing on a router

questions.explanation: 2000::/3 global unicast, fe80::/10 link-local, fc00::/7 unique local (fd00::/8 in use), ff00::/8 multicast (ff02::5 is OSPFv3 all routers), ::1 loopback. NDP replaces ARP; LANs use /64; ipv6 unicast-routing turns the router on for IPv6 forwarding.
